## Failing test case(s) - `options/verify-dbot-login-from-dbot.spec.ts` → **VERIFY user can login from DBot and navigate back to home** (webkit) - TestDino case: `d13e8b54476c8d39bdf7-05abbb2dd8f619bbfa32` - Failing run: [GitHub Actions run ](https://github.com/deriv-com/home-app/actions/runs/, branch `main`, commit `5aa332921bccd7b2ca61534d6bcb9b6cd05789f9`) - Group: `010-ui-change-1f598fe8e668` (single-candidate group) ## What is failing `LoginPage.waitForEmailPageToLoad()` (`playwright/pages/LoginPage.ts:383`) throws a Playwright **strict-mode violation**: ``` Error: locator.waitFor: Error: strict mode violation: getByRole('heading', { level: 1 }) resolved to 3 elements: 1)

Welcome to Deriv Bot!

2)

Guide

3)

FAQs

``` This is a **test-side race condition, not a product regression**. `DBotPage.clickLoginButton()` clicked the DBot header "Log in" button and returned immediately, without waiting for the cross-origin SSO redirect to the home-app `/login` page to actually complete. The test then immediately called `loginPage.enterEmailAndSubmit()` → `waitForEmailPageToLoad()`, which ran its `getByRole('heading', { level: 1 })` check while the browser was still showing the **DBot dashboard** — specifically its "Welcome to Deriv Bot!" guide panel, which renders three of its own `

` headings ("Welcome to Deriv Bot!", "Guide", "FAQs"). Playwright's strict-mode check is a hard, immediately-thrown error (unlike a "not visible" wait condition), so it fails the instant more than one `

` is present — even transiently, before the real navigation lands. This is corroborated across **both attempts** of the failing run (initial + retry1): both show the identical error, and both attempts' captured accessibility-tree snapshots (`error-context.md`) show only the correct single `heading "Welcome back" [level=1]` once the page had settled — proving the login page itself is correct and unchanged; the failure window is purely transient. `LoginPage.welcomeBackHeading` (`getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })`, unscoped) is deliberately language-agnostic per its own doc comment, to support non-English locale test runs — narrowing it to match `"Welcome back"` text would be an incorrect, coverage-breaking fix that could break other (non-English) callers. It is used by ~15 other spec files across `auth/`, `deriv-pay/`, `options/`, and `profile/`, so it was left untouched. ## Evidence - `error-context.md` (attempt 0) and `error-context.md` (retry1) — identical strict-mode violation and source location (`LoginPage.ts:383`) on both attempts. - `test-failed-1.png` (attempt 0) — screenshot shows the browser still rendering the **DBot Dashboard** (Dashboard/Bot Builder/Charts/Tutorials tabs, "Load or build your bot" panel) with the "Welcome to Deriv Bot!" guide panel open on the right — the visual source of the three matched `

` elements — confirming navigation to the login page had not yet completed at the moment of failure. - `DBotPage.clickLoginButton()` only special-cases dismissing the "Welcome to Deriv Bot!" panel on mobile (`if (this.isMobile)`); on desktop (webkit — our failing viewport) no dismissal runs, and more importantly, the method never waited for the SSO redirect to actually land before returning control to the caller. - Compared `DTraderPage.clickLoginButton()` and `SmartTraderPage.clickLoginButton()` (same "click login button on an external embedded app" pattern) — both share the identical missing-navigation-wait shape. No failure evidence exists for either in this run/group, so per the minimal-fix mandate only the evidenced `DBotPage` caller was changed. - Existing codebase precedent for this exact pattern: `SignupPage.ts:812` already does `await this.page.waitForURL(/\/login(\/|\?|$)/);` after an action that triggers a redirect to the login page. ## Changes - `playwright/pages/DBotPage.ts` — `clickLoginButton()` now waits for the browser to actually navigate to `/login` (`await this.page.waitForURL(/\/login(\/|\?|$)/);`) after clicking, before returning control to the caller. This closes the race: `waitForEmailPageToLoad()` can no longer run against the still-current DBot page. - No changes to `LoginPage.ts`, other page objects, `playwright/flows/**`, or `src/`. ## Verification Playwright CLI could not be executed in this environment (all `npx playwright` invocations required interactive approval that was unavailable in this session) — classified as **Cannot run CLI** per the `fix-testdino-test-case` skill's Phase 7. The fix was verified by static/visual analysis only: re-reading the corrected `clickLoginButton()` against both failing attempts' evidence and the established `waitForURL(/\/login.../)` pattern used elsewhere in the codebase (`SignupPage.ts:812`). Recommend a human/CI run of `TEST_ENV=staging npx playwright test --project=webkit options/verify-dbot-login-from-dbot.spec.ts` to confirm before merge. > [!NOTE] > This PR was opened after the healer agent's sample Playwright CLI verification (pass, or original signature fixed with an unrelated/downstream failure). Review the diff before merging.

## Failing test case(s)

- `crypto-exchange/verify-exchange-deposit-deriv-wallet.spec.ts` › `Crypto Exchange — Deposit via Deriv Wallet` › `VERIFY USD Wallet row is excluded from the deposit coin list` (chromium, chromium-mobile)
- `crypto-exchange/verify-exchange-deposit-deriv-wallet.spec.ts` › `Crypto Exchange — Deposit via Deriv Wallet` › `VERIFY deposit via USDT_<Network> wallet skips network picker and completes` (same shell assertion, same POM method — verified as a second call site sharing the fix)

## What is failing

`CryptoExchangePage.verifyDepositCoinListVisible()` asserted only `depositCoinListPicker` (`exchange-deposit-wallet-picker`) was visible. The product code (`src/features/crypto-exchange/components/shared/crypto-exchange-wallet-coin-list.tsx`) renders the picker and a "Deposit paused" rate-unavailable screen (`exchange-deposit-wallet-rate-unavailable`) as **mutually exclusive** branches of one ternary, based on `marketDataError`. When the rate-unavailable branch rendered, the picker never appeared, and the assertion hard-failed after its 45s timeout with `element(s) not found` — even though the screen was fully rendered and not a loading state.

This regressed when the rate-unavailable screen was added to the product code (commit `1d8f71b13`, <redacted-phone>). A later commit (`fafbc384e`, <redacted-phone>) added the POM's `depositRateUnavailable` locator and a proper skip-on-`rate_unavailable` branch in `waitForDepositCoinListItemsLoaded()`, and even documented `verifyDepositCoinListVisible()` as "shell-only" in its own JSDoc — but never updated the assertion itself to accept the rate-unavailable render, leaving the shell check unable to reach that already-correct skip logic.

## Evidence

- CI artifact (`error-context.md` + `test-failed-1.png`) for the failing run shows the accessibility tree and screenshot in a fully-rendered "Deposit paused / Deposits are temporarily unavailable. Try again later. / Got it" state at the moment of failure — not a loading skeleton.
- `src/features/crypto-exchange/components/shared/crypto-exchange-wallet-coin-list.tsx`: `isRateUnavailable ? <...-rate-unavailable> : <...-picker>` — confirms the two states can never coexist.
- Only two call sites of `verifyDepositCoinListVisible()` exist in `playwright/`, both in this spec, both already followed by the correct `loadState !== "rows"` skip branch that this fix unblocks.

## Changes

`playwright/pages/CryptoExchangePage.ts` — `verifyDepositCoinListVisible()` now asserts `this.depositCoinListPicker.or(this.depositRateUnavailable)` instead of the picker alone, matching the mutually-exclusive rendering in product code. JSDoc updated to explain why.

Verified locally against staging: both affected tests (`chromium-mobile` and `chromium`) now run to completion — the shell assertion passes and each test proceeds to its pre-existing `test.skip()` gate instead of hard-failing at the picker-visibility timeout.

## Summary

GTM-NF7884S injects Bing UET, Snapchat Pixel, LinkedIn Insight, and AdRoll after `gtm.js` boots. Those script hosts were missing from `script-src-elem`, so Chromium blocked them on every page load (observed on staging `/set-password`) and the pixels collected nothing.

Same class of drift as #3251 (Yandex / Google Ads / LinkedIn **image** beacons): allow the script **and** the transport host, otherwise you just swap a load error for a transmit error.

## Changes

- Allow `bat.bing.com`, `sc-static.net`, `snap.licdn.com`, and `d.adroll.com` in `script-src` / `script-src-elem`
- Allow the matching event hosts in `connect-src`: `bat.bing.com`, `tr.snapchat.com`, `px.ads.linkedin.com`, `d.adroll.com`
- Allow the noscript / image-pixel fallbacks in `img-src`: `bat.bing.com`, `tr.snapchat.com`, `d.adroll.com`
- Extend `content-security-policy.test.ts` so these hosts cannot drift again

`s.adroll.com` was already allowlisted. CSP host matching is exact, so it does not cover `d.adroll.com`.

- [ ] New feature

body: ## Summary Three third-party conversion pixels are blocked by CSP on every page load, dominating the console on the signup funnel (`/dashboard/verify-email`, `/dashboard/set-password`) with `The action has been blocked.` errors. All three fire their beacon as an `` GET, and an image fetch consults `img-src` only — it never falls back to `connect-src`. This adds the three hosts to `img-src`, plus regression assertions so it cannot silently come back. ### Root-cause hypothesis `next.config.ts`, the `img-src` directive in the `csp` array inside `headers()`. | Host | `script-src` | `connect-src` | `img-src` (before) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `https://mc.yandex.ru` | yes | yes | **no** | | `https://www.googleadservices.com` | yes | yes | **no** | | `https://px.ads.linkedin.com` | no (GTM-injected) | no | **no** | This is the "tag loads but its transport is refused" trap already documented in the `connect-src` header comments and asserted against in `src/lib/config/content-security-policy.test.ts`. The tag boots because `script-src` allows it, then the beacon it emits is blocked. For Yandex this is a **partial-fix regression**: c21b3b117 (PR #3229, issue #3228) added the host to `connect-src` for the webvisor `fetch()` uploads and the `wss://` socket only. The `/metrika/advert.gif` image beacon uses the image fetch classifier and stayed blocked. The CSP header is global (`/(.*)`, and reused verbatim for the relaxed `frame-ancestors` variant), so the defect is not page-specific — the signup steps just fire the most marketing tags per load, which is why the report reads as flow-specific when it isn't. Nothing in lint, typecheck or the build can see this: the CSP is a plain template string. That is exactly why the assertions belong in the CSP test file. ### Deliberately NOT changed: `https://snap.licdn.com` The report asks to *consider* adding it to `script-src` / `connect-src`. Not done, on purpose. The only observed evidence is the `px.ads.linkedin.com/collect` image beacon, and its `tm=gtmv2` parameter marks it as fired directly by GTM's LinkedIn Insight template rather than by a loaded `insight.min.js`; no `snap.licdn.com` violation was reported. Widening `script-src` — the most security-sensitive directive in the policy — on speculation is the wrong trade. If RUM or DevTools later shows a real block there, it is a one-line follow-up with evidence behind it. ## Changes - `next.config.ts` — added `https://mc.yandex.ru`, `https://www.googleadservices.com` and `https://px.ads.linkedin.com` to `img-src`. Explicit hosts only, no wildcard widening, one comment per host matching the surrounding style (and recording *why* each needs `img-src` specifically, given two of them are already in `connect-src`). - `src/lib/config/content-security-policy.test.ts` — three table-driven assertions that each host is permitted by `img-src` in **every** emitted policy, using the file's existing CSP host matcher (real host matching, not substring grep). ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] UI / design update - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs / skills update ## TDD evidence Test committed first (1ad4b763d), implementation second (b2d5a47b4). Polarity not inverted — the same three assertions fail before and pass after. **Red** — `1ad4b763d`, test only, production code untouched: ``` ✓ ... emits a policy on every configured route source ✓ ... allows https://mc.yandex.ru in connect-src, since the tag is allowlisted in script-src ✓ ... allows wss://mc.yandex.ru in connect-src, since the tag is allowlisted in script-src ✓ ... keeps script-src and script-src-elem in agreement about the tag × ... allows the https://mc.yandex.ru conversion beacon in img-src × ... allows the https://www.googleadservices.com conversion beacon in img-src × ... allows the https://px.ads.linkedin.com conversion beacon in img-src Test Files 1 failed (1) Tests 3 failed | 4 passed (7) ``` **Green** — after `b2d5a47b4`: ``` ✓ src/lib/config/content-security-policy.test.ts (7 tests) 6ms Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 7 passed (7) ``` ## Test plan - [x] `npm run test` — 3362 passed / 355 files, full suite green locally (CI is the gate). - [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean. - [x] `npm run lint` — 0 errors (49 pre-existing warnings, none in the touched files). - [ ] **Reviewer check on the PR preview:** open DevTools → Console on `/dashboard/verify-email` and `/dashboard/set-password` and confirm the three `img-src` violations are gone. This cannot be verified from CI — the beacons only fire against a real GTM container. - [ ] **Reviewer sanity check:** confirm no *new* blocked host appears once the pixels start succeeding (the `snap.licdn.com` question above). ## Playwright impact: None. Static analysis only — this runner cannot execute the Playwright suite (it needs `ENV_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, the `e2e-tests-core` submodule and a live staging backend), so **no Playwright spec was run**. A grep across `playwright/` for `content-security|csp|img-src| yandex|googleadservices|px.ads` returns nothing: no spec asserts on response headers or console errors. The change touches only an HTTP response header — no route, copy, `data-testid`, or user-visible behaviour — so no spec's assertions are invalidated. No i18n, `data-testid` or Quill considerations: no user-facing strings and no UI elements are added or modified. ## Screenshots n/a — no UI change. ## Related issues / PRs Closes #3250 Related: #3229 / #3228 — the earlier Yandex `connect-src` fix this completes. slack-thread:
title: fix(csp): allow the Yandex, Google Ads and LinkedIn conversion beacons in img-src
